_notes: The overnight state for the Underdog run. Fired by the Autopilot holding step at curtain+210 (23:00 evenings, 20:30 on Sunday 27 September) and held until the preshow loop starts again at curtain-30. Rebuilt 18 September 2026 to David's brief: the foyer screen is visible from the street after the building is locked, so this phase is a black panel with one small white status line in the top-left corner and nothing else - no show wordmark, no brand mark, no ambient wash. It advertises nothing, including itself. The blackout is in style.css under body[data-phase="holding"]; the line is whatever the item below resolves to.
_show_when_note: Items carry show_when: "countdown" (there is a future performance), "final" (there is not), or "always". Each case now has exactly one card, so the phase is a single line either way. The three final-night cards that advertised Shakespeare in Love and the club nights were removed on 18 September: they were the display talking to an empty, locked foyer at midnight, which is what this phase is meant to avoid. They are in git history if the end of the run ever wants a send-off.
_policy_note: One card, refreshed every 60 seconds - consecutive_repeat is true because there is nothing to alternate with and the refresh exists solely to advance the countdown. max_words_per_screen drops to 12: anything longer than a status line does not belong here.

items._note: The overnight line. Small white text, top left, on black. 'message' is only the fallback for the case where performances.json cannot be read and no countdown can be worked out.
items._countdown_format_note: {countdown} renders with units - '20h 00m', '1d 22h 30m' - never a bare H:MM. Measured 15 September: on four of the six nights the gap from bar close to the next house opening is exactly 20 hours, and 'resumes in 20:00' at midnight reads as 'resumes at eight o'clock'. The Sunday gap is 46h 30m, which as '46:30' means nothing at all.

items._note: After the last performance there is no countdown to show, so the line states the fact and stops. Same small white text, same black screen.
